This project tests classical computer vision on {n_strips} fabric strips.
Strips are cut into overlapping patches. Split by patch, and test texture leaks into training.
So I split by whole strip, and held out entire fabrics.
Each patch gets ninety texture features. Supervised models learn defects. Anomaly detectors learn only normal fabric.
Everything is scored three ways, including a deliberately leaky control.
For the random forest, patch precision is {rf_ap_grouped} split by strip, and {rf_ap_leaky} with leaky patches. A paired difference of plus {gap}, interval {gap_lo} to {gap_hi}.
On an unseen fabric, nothing clearly beats chance. The best of eight methods scores {unseen}, interval {unseen_lo} to {unseen_hi}.
Every strip can be inspected. Here are the forest's misses.
Some results look good for the wrong reasons. Brightness alone reaches {bright_auc} within one fabric. Those strips were captured differently.
The limits are real: one small dataset, {n_fabrics} fabrics, precomputed results, no factory testing.
{margin_strips} of {n_strips} strips also have blank margins.
Code, tables and the explorer are all open.
